newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - BTP vol slips as EMU hopes rebound.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - BTP vol slips as EMU hopes rebound.

text.p: Implied volatility of Italian BTP options slid on Friday, as expectations increased that the forthcoming Amsterdam summit will put plans for a single European currency back on track, traders in London said.

European Commission President Jacques Santer said he believed Europe would be able to agree on a budget pact next week -- as long as it also stepped up the fight for jobs and intensified policy co-ordination.
However, analysts said there was too much optimism that European bonds would remain unruffled priced into the market.

"European volatilities are a buy at the moment," said Andy Ash, derivatives analyst at Monument Derivatives in London. "People are relaxed about being short while the markets are behaving so well. But I think it's unlikely BTPs will be at this level in a week's time."
September BTP futures were at 131.38, down 25 basis points by 1000 GMT.

France's new Socialist-led government threw a spanner in the euro works when it said it needed more time to consider the stability pact, aimed at assuring fiscal restraint following the introduction of the single currency.

Implied volatility of the at-the-money September BTP option was at 7.7 to 7.9 percent, down from 7.8 to 8.02 on Thursday. December dipped to 7.93-8.04 percent compared with 8.0-8.34 in the prior session.
A trader at a British brokerage said activity was relatively light so far this session, with the largest trade in the 134.00 strike calls.

He said the Franco-German summit between German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and President Jacques Chirac and the new French government, to discuss the EU budget pact, was expected to underline the political commitment to monetary union.

"A lot of the U.S. investors particularly think that Europe has travelled so far down the road that it can't turn back," the trader said. "It seems to them that EMU is a party that everyone is invited to."
